title: China-to-North Macedonia EV Charger Compliance Gap Matrix
provenance: AI-compiled, multi-model cross-checked, not human-verified. Informational only; confirm with the official regulator and a qualified professional. Not legal/certification/customs/market-access advice.

rows.requirement: Connector Redesign — IEC 62196 Type 2 and CCS2
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia EV charging deployment follows European IEC interoperability practice for most public and semi-public charging: IEC 62196 Type 2 for AC charging and CCS Combo 2 for DC where the charging model and vehicle fleet specify it. Connector selection is a technical interoperability and procurement requirement, not standalone legal market approval.
target_standards: Project, fleet, operator, or public-procurement connector requirements
rows.china_equivalent: China typically uses GB/T 20234.2 for AC connection devices, GB/T 20234.3 for DC interfaces, and GB/T 27930 for DC charger-to-BMS communication. Those materials should not be treated as Type 2 or CCS2 readiness without hardware, cable, pilot signal, locking, PLC/CAN, labeling, and safety re-evaluation.
rows.gap: GB/T-only chargers need a hardware and protocol conversion plan for North Macedonia-facing projects: Type 2 or CCS2 couplers, cable thermal rating, lock and proximity circuits, control-pilot behaviour, DC PLC communication where CCS2 is used, charger labels, spare-part list, and retesting after connector redesign.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where intended North Macedonia deployment, procurement document, charging network, or vehicle fleet specifies Type 2 / CCS2; otherwise market interoperability expectation rather than standalone approval
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 20234 conformity is a China-market connector baseline and is not a substitute for Type 2 or CCS2 compatibility

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not describe a GB/T 20234 connector package as Type 2 or CCS2 ready. Connector hardware, communications, labels, and safety evidence should be rebuilt around the specified IEC interface for the intended North Macedonia deployment.

rows.requirement: ERC Charging-Service Licensing and MEPSO Grid Project Review
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia regulates public charging-service market activity through ERC frameworks, including licensing routes, electronic transactions, charging automation, and market access controls. Grid-side installation and energisation can also involve MEPSO project approval and acceptance processes plus the relevant distribution company.
target_standards: North Macedonia charging and energy transformation regulation
EPDK-like licensing pattern in North Macedonia market practice
MEPSO project approval and acceptance processes
rows.china_equivalent: China GB/T charger test reports and CCC or voluntary certification files address product conformity and do not replace a North Macedonia charging-network operator licence, automation interface process, MEPSO project approval, or local distribution-company energisation procedure.
china_standards: China charger certification files where applicable
rows.gap: Separate product readiness from service-operation readiness. The North Macedonia operator package may need licence-holder details, station registration data, backend integration, site electrical project documents, MEPSO correspondence, metering and tariff data, commissioning records, and local maintenance responsibilities.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory for entities carrying out licensed public charging-network operation where ERC charging-service rules apply; MEPSO and distribution-company review is mandatory where the site electrical project and grid-connection route requires it
mandatory_status.cn: Chinese product conformity files do not create North Macedonia charging-service, grid-connection, or operation rights

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] A CE or GB/T product file does not authorise public charging-service operation in North Macedonia. Confirm the ERC licence holder, automation obligations, MEPSO project approval route, and distribution-company energisation steps for each site.

rows.requirement: North Macedonia CE Marking and TS EN IEC 61851 Safety File
rows.target_requirement: North Macedonia-market EV charging equipment should be prepared with a CE-style technical file, declaration of conformity, marking, installation manual, and risk assessment for the applicable EU-aligned product legislation. IEC 61851-1:2017 is the core conductive charging system safety standard and covers operating conditions, EVSE-to-vehicle connection, and electrical safety requirements. The local route should be checked with ISRSM catalogue adoption and project or purchaser requirements.
target_standards: CE marking for applicable EU-aligned product legislation
TS EN IEC 61851 series, ISRSM catalogue adoption to be verified
rows.china_equivalent: China commonly uses GB/T 18487.1 for conductive charging system requirements and GB/T 20234 for connection devices. Those files help map technical clauses but do not replace a North Macedonia CE technical file, declaration, North Macedonia-language installation documentation, or TS EN IEC 61851 review where required.
rows.gap: Convert China documentation into a CE-style technical file for North Macedonia: applicable directive mapping, harmonised or adopted standard list, test reports, drawings, critical component certificates, risk analysis, North Macedonia language installation and safety instructions, declaration of conformity, label artwork, and change-control evidence.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where the charger falls under CE-marked electrical or electronic product legislation; TS EN IEC 61851 is a technical conformity route or project requirement unless a local rule makes the exact route mandatory for the model
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 18487 and GB/T 20234 are common China technical baselines; domestic mandatory certification status must be checked for the exact charger category and effective date

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Treat IEC / TS EN IEC 61851 evidence as part of a North Macedonia CE technical-file route, not as standalone market-access approval. Confirm ISRSM adoption and any purchaser or project requirement before claiming market readiness.

source.publisher: Standardization Institute of the Republic of North Macedonia (ISRSM)

rows.target_requirement: OCPP is the open communication protocol between charging stations and charging management systems. OCPP 1.6, OCPP 2.0.1, and OCPP 2.1 are used internationally; OCPP 2.0.1 edition 3 was approved as IEC 63584 in 2024 and OCPP 2.1 in 2025. North Macedonia projects may require OCPP through operator backend, automation, tender, roaming, payment, maintenance, and grid-interaction specifications even when OCPP is not the whole-unit product approval route.
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese DC chargers commonly rely on GB/T 27930 for charger-to-vehicle communication. That protocol is not an operator backend protocol and does not replace OCPP implementation, cybersecurity profiles, backend acceptance testing, remote firmware update procedures, or operator data interfaces.
rows.gap: The North Macedonia project file should identify exact OCPP version, security profile, certificate handling, meter-value mapping, transaction model, remote reset and firmware process, SIM or Ethernet architecture, local operator endpoint, and test evidence from the target charging management system.

mandatory_status.target: Usually mandatory when required by the operator, tender, automation integration, roaming, payment, maintenance, or grid-interaction specification; OCPP is not by itself a whole-unit safety certification
mandatory_status.cn: GB/T 27930 is vehicle-side DC charging communication and does not satisfy backend OCPP requirements

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Confirm OCPP version and security profile with the North Macedonia operator before shipment. GB/T 27930 support does not prove backend interoperability with ERC-facing or operator-facing charging management systems.

rows.requirement: EMC, Low-Voltage Safety, and Residual-Current Protection
rows.target_requirement: EV chargers placed on North Macedonia CE-aligned market normally need conformity evidence for applicable electrical safety and EMC legislation. For EVSE, IEC 61851-1 includes EVSE electrical-safety requirements; EMC evidence is mapped separately to the applicable EMC route and charger-specific EMC test standard. Residual-current protection, DC residual-current detection, protective earthing, overcurrent protection, surge protection, and installation coordination should be documented for final site design.
target_standards: Directive 2014/35/EU Low Voltage Directive, North Macedonia implementation to be verified
Directive 2014/30/EU EMC Directive, North Macedonia implementation to be verified
IEC 61851-21-2 EMC route for off-board EV charging systems, current edition to be verified
rows.china_equivalent: Chinese files may include GB/T 18487.1 safety evidence, GB/T 18487.2 EMC evidence for off-board conductive supply equipment, component certificates, and site electrical drawings. These should be clause-mapped and retested where needed for North Macedonia CE, IEC / EN, site-earthing, RCD, and installation assumptions.
rows.gap: The gap is often in installation assumptions rather than lab reports: earthing system, upstream breaker, RCD type or RDC-DD arrangement, DC leakage handling, EMC cable routing, surge protection, short-circuit rating, enclosure IP/IK, ambient rating, and North Macedonia-language warnings should match the actual deployment.

mandatory_status.target: Mandatory where applicable CE-aligned low-voltage and EMC legislation applies; RCD and installation protection are mandatory where required by the applicable installation design, grid connection, or electrical code route
mandatory_status.cn: China GB/T safety and EMC evidence supports comparison but does not replace North Macedonia CE and site-installation verification

rows.verdict: [INFORMATIONAL] Do not rely on a China EMC or safety report without checking North Macedonia CE scope, IEC / EN test coverage, and the real site protection design. RCD, earthing, leakage detection, and EMC installation assumptions should be documented before commissioning.
